title: Wave Function Collapse in Quantum Theory
text:
Superposition dictates that a quantum particle, such as an electron, exists in all possible states simultaneously until it is measured. This inherent property means the system is described by a wave function, which contains probabilities for various outcomes rather than specifying a single fixed location or momentum.

The measurement problem is defined by the transition from this probabilistic superposition to a definite classical reality upon observation. The act of measurement forces the wave function to 'collapse,' selecting one particular state from the multitude of possibilities. This abrupt change remains a core area of investigation in modern physics, leading to various interpretations regarding the fundamental nature of reality and the role of the observer.
